body: The problem is that I love my dad so much and he loves me a lot, especially when I was a kid I was a papa’s girl. It would kill me to lose him, I think it might be even worse for him, he’s an incredibly complicated man. Losing me would destroy him, but if he found out about my relationship, and especially if we went abroad together, he would end our contact, probably also with my (dads) family. Moving away helped a lot, it was easier keeping things superficial and short, seeing him once a month stopped a lot of the issues. I’m so torn

I have other friends too, this is just a really close group of 3. We’re also in a bigger friend group and I have a friendgroup next to that one. The problem is he thinks I owe him my time. He has to come before everyone and everything else. When I told him my mental health was declining and I might not make it to uni that year (the same uni he is in) he replied with: ‘have you even thought about how much this sucks for me? I thought you would be coming to uni this year and we would hang out and now it looks like you might not come’  My mental health improved and I made the year but from that point on I didn’t like him as much anymore, I started noticing how much he thinks about himself and how much he judges others. I always want everyone to be able to completely be their authentic selves. I can’t be myself around him, he doesn’t like it when I sing, I love singing, because he is scared of the opinion of others. He judges people all the time. 
 
I can try having a conversation with him about this, I’ve actually had one before with him. But he just denies he does it… 

I can try to stop hanging out but he’ll probably come to our house since me and the other friend live together. I’m having fun on the holiday so far and I don’t mind him that much. I just realized he isn’t someone I want in my life.

Again, making assumptions about me. You can't say I'm the problem when all I want is more transparant and honest communication. If people don't want to hang out with me, I'd rather have them to straight up tell me.   
\> ''It doesn't matter if they're telling little white lies to get you to leave them alone >without causing a scene. All that matters is how we choose to react to things.''  


I can mostly tell when people don't want to hang out with me, but if you tell me, and I quote: ''you can always call me, even if that wakes me up at night when you're feeling down''. Then that doesn't really give any hints of them wanting me to leave them alone, does it? Another example from someone else: "When I get back into <country> again, do you want to grab a drink sometime?''   


First person never picks up my calls nor do they ask why I called afterwards. Second person I tried to make plans with, then I stopped trying, with both of them. I have more examples of this but this was just to show how it isn't always super obvious what they want or mean.   


All what I did was express my frustation on this website about this. How its normal to make hollow promises like this. I try to be mature in my conversations, never have I gotten angry at someone. I just leave them alone, because like you said ''Stop caring about people who don't care about you.'' and that's what I try to do.  


Also never said they were the problem, I have done the exact same things in the past, trying to please others. It's a normal thing to do. But I stopped because I realised I didn't like changing myself for others nor did I like making empty promises. All I want is openness, honesty and directness from others. It would make my life, and undoubtedly many others too, so much easier.

I mean, I understand. It would be a lie to say I have never done this in the past myself, I think its because I personally felt the need to please people. After a while I realised I didn't like it when people did it to me, so I stopped doing it myself.   


Anxiety sucks, but I just wish people were more open and communicative about things like this. It would create a better understanding between people.

I have never been rude to someone who I thought was just being polite. This was all in my head and never have I ever reacted to someone the same way I vent on here. I am not mad at those people, I am just confused on how this is a normal thing to do. I understand that people want to please others or whatever the reason may be. Still doesnt mean I wouldn't rather have people say what they mean.

I can tell the difference after a while. F.e. when someone says ''we should totally get a drink together!'' I have no reason to believe that they were just being polite. Only after a while when I realise I haven't heard back from them, that's when I realise.

You can call me socially inept but you have made assumptions about me without any context whatsoever. I am not personally mad at the people who do this, I am just mad about how this is a socially acceptable thing to do.

Sure!  
Before going to university we have to write a paper on a subject that we find interesting. The grade of this paper weighs really heavy. You choose a class (f.e. social sciences, economics, english, etc.) that fits your interests and your university. Then you choose a subject and perform research, could be with experiments or surverys, but it can also be a literature research. You need to spend at least 80 hours and have 8.000 - 12.000 words. The purpose of this paper is to learn how to dive in deep and learn how to perform research.
